title.narrative: Reducing methane emissions through an integrated data approach

description.narrative: Contract related to: Reducing methane emissions through an integrated data approach - The action aims to accelerate reductions of methane emissions by integrating and reconciling emissions data sources, linking findings to ambitious action, and supporting the science-policy interface. It will do by supporting the activities of the International Methane Emission Observatory (IMEO) with a view to increase the use of data by governments and companies in order to design and adopt methane emission mitigation strategies and targets. 15 to update and 5 to develop

Technical Guidance DocumentsBy December 2023 the Partnership has developed 19 Technical Guidance Documents TGDs supporting companies in addressing OGMP 2.0 reporting requirements across the five reporting levels for the most material sources of methane emissions including 3 additional Technical Guidance Documents finalized in 2023 for the LNG value chain liquefaction shipping and regasification.Each Technical Guidance Document provides a brief description of the emission sources the system boundaries Level 3 emission factors and Level 4 Direct measurement and Measurementbased Emission factors quantification methodologies. One of the 19 TGDs presents general principles that apply to all the OGMP Technical Guidance Documents and one is devoted to reporting at Level 1 and 2.All 19 TGDs are living documents that are updated as new data and technologies become available. Based on a discussion within the Partnership the current TGDs will be updated following a public consultation to be launched in 2024 to integrate learnings from companies reporting in 2024 when over 60 companies are expected to report at the most granular Level 4 and Level 5 to reach the Gold Standard Reporting.Uncertainty and Reconciliation Guidance DocumentIn 2023 the OGMP 2.0 also developed an Uncertainty and Reconciliation Guidance document offering considerations for operators to approach L4 inventory and L5 estimate development including the process of reconciliation. In addition the Partnership produced a guidance on the documentation requirements list of information elements that a company should provide for Level 4 and Level 5 reporting building on the Uncertainty and Reconciliation Guidance.OGMP 2.0 Reporting TemplatesThe OGMP 2.0 reporting templates one for upstream and one for mid and downstream segment where companies list and report emissions from their operated and nonoperated assets were updated in 2023 together with their associated guidance documents that provide a stepbystep support for companies to use in submitting methane emissions from all assets under scope.Implementation Plan TemplateUNEP issued a nonmandatory template as a tool that companies can adopt in preparing their annual implementation plan including all the required elements.Coal Technical Guidance DocumentsTwo coal TGDs Ventilation Air Methane Vented and Drained Coal Mine Methane Vented were developed by UNEP in August 2023 but not yet published.Additional guidance under developmentDifferent OGMP 2.0 technical task forces restarted their work in 2023 to develop additional guidance on e.g. Joint Venture Engagement operational guidance on Level 4 and Level 5 reporting new Technical Guidance Documents on well drilling and other well eventsinterventions. This work is in progress and expected to be finalized in 2024.

comment.narrative: In 2023 IMEO undertook dedicated projects mainly in Turkmenistan Nigeria and Iraq. IMEO worked with the UN Resident Coordinator in Turkmenistan to raise awareness on methane emissions with the government and to share satellite data through MARS. IMEO is working in collaboration with the EU Delegation in Nigeria to conduct a measurement study and build capacity in government and research communities. In collaboration with the IEA Clean Air Task Force and CCAC IMEO is contributing satellite analysis and training to a joint proposal to develop a methane inventory assessment and mitigation options to the government of Iraq.

comment.narrative: IMEO has been entrusted by the Global Methane Pledge GMP to create a sound scientific basis for methane emissions calculations. IMEO is committed to delivering accurate and reliable calculations that will help reduce methane emissions by at least 30 from 2020 levels by 2030 as per the GMPs goal.Under the GMP IMEO has launched the Methane Alert and Response System MARS to scale up the detection of major emission events notify relevant stakeholders and support and track mitigation progress. Through the MARS project the government of the following 13 countries have received notifications providing information on methane emissions Argentina Egypt Iran Iraq Kazakhstan Mexico Qatar United States Uzbekistan Angola Mozambique Malaysia Oman.In 2023 13 Countries have been equipped with accurate methane data through science studies Angola Gabon Algeria Venezuela US Norway UK Netherlands Germany France Romania Mexico Australia.IMEO Science studies focus on regions andor sources where there is limited or not publicly available empirically based data and provide the understanding necessary to guide mitigation action.IMEO is currently coordinating with local representatives from oil and gas companies governments potential institutional partners as well as with its scientific network to identify gaps and determine the objectives of each new study that needs to be conducted.
